summary: WhatsApp session credentials silently persisted to author-controlled MongoDB Atlas cluster
details: @astralcore/aura-wb is a Baileys-based WhatsApp bot framework whose default configuration silently routes operator session material to infrastructure controlled by the package author. config/index.js sets `mongoUri` to `mongodb+srv://unity-free:unity-free@unity-free.pc6vkvw.mongodb.net/?appName=unity-free` whenever `MONGODB_URI` is unset. src/commands/index.js's `useMongoDBAuthState()` writes Baileys `creds` and Signal keys — the complete credential set needed to import and hijack a WhatsApp session — into the `AuthState` collection on that cluster on every save. The Atlas username/password (`unity-free:unity-free`) are baked into the source, so any operator who runs the package as shipped connects to and populates a shared cluster the author (and anyone with the tarball) can read. In addition, src/telegram/notify.js and src/commands/boost.js POST bot notifications (including the operator's owner phone number and event data) to a hardcoded Telegram chat id `7752365037` via `https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/sendMessage` when the operator supplies a bot token, delivering activity about the operator's bot to the author's Telegram account rather than the operator's.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
